verdict.rationale: PlanetScale's own docs describe branching database schemas like code branches, plus deploy requests that ship non-blocking schema changes to production with zero downtime. A community user corroborates the per-Git-branch database workflow, but another notes that the non-blocking schema change workflow does not support foreign keys. Missing for 10: foreign key support in the non-blocking workflow, documented deploy-request or online-DDL detail for the Postgres side (Postgres branching is only shown for development and testing), and in-depth evidence of the locking-avoidance mechanism or a revert path.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ship schema changes safely — online DDL, deploy requests, or branch-and-merge workflows — without locking or breaking production

citations.quote: Database branching, coupled with deploy requests, allows you to deploy non-blocking schema changes to your production database with zero downtime.
PlanetScale allows you to branch database schemas the same way you branch your code.
You can then create development branches that you can use for development before shipping schema changes to production.
It will give you a database branch for each Git branch and help you manage the workflows around it.
